topics.label: Cancer therapy lecture framing and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students, introduces the lecture subject, and states what they should learn.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: Both are treatments directed at a tumour mass or site, removing it surgically or damaging its DNA with radiation.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms, efficacy, toxicity and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs kill cancer cells, their clinical benefits, and the limitations that arise from toxicity and resistance.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how blocking hormonal signals can restrain cancers that still depend on those signals for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how cancer cells with defective checkpoint proteins can be selectively exploited, first through irradiation and then through oncolytic adenoviruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inhibiting PARP can create lethal DNA damage in cancer cells that lack BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapy and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop the strategy of targeting oncogenic drivers, explain how kinase inhibitors work, and show how resistance limits their effects.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody-based cancer treatments
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics use antibodies to recognize cell-surface proteins and focus an inhibitory, immune, or cytotoxic effect on the targeted cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic weighs evidence for and against a protective role for the immune system in controlling cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics address how checkpoint inhibition enables antitumour T-cell responses and how neoantigen burden can affect those responses.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells to cancer with bispecific engagers and CAR T cells
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches bring T-cell cytotoxic activity to cancer cells through engineered recognition, using either a bispecific molecule or modified T cells.

topics.label: Cancer therapy challenges and personalised treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic gathers the limitations of cancer treatment around the challenge of matching therapies to patients and managing tumour heterogeneity.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends and prevention
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers changes in cancer incidence and outcomes while explaining why prevention and early detection complicate attribution to treatment.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers how cancer care might develop while weighing treatment possibilities against patient quality of life and difficult clinical choices.

topics.label: Childhood leukaemia survival and the dilemma of testing targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: This closing example contrasts major gains in childhood leukaemia survival with the difficulty of testing new targeted drugs against a proven treatment.
